original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Income and Outlays release for August 2026 published September 30, 2026 at 08:30 ET. Resolve TRUE if the seasonally adjusted PCE price index excluding food and energy month-over-month change for August is 0.3% or higher at the precision shown in that first release; otherwise FALSE. Score p=0.62 with Brier and log loss. Score the 0.3% point by absolute error against the same first-release value and the frozen 0.3% external-consensus point; record whether the first-release value lies inside the 0.1%-0.5% 80% interval. The annual methodology update and revisions to prior months may inform later model state but must not alter this target, threshold or score after publication. Do not substitute later revisions.
rationale: The current H003/H001 split is close enough that a monthly core-price realization is more discriminating than Monday's causally ambiguous yield/equity response.

July first-release core PCE was +0.2% m/m, while August core CPI was +0.3% and August final-demand PPI was +0.4%; these inputs make a 0.3% core-PCE print plausible without supporting a high-confidence hot-inflation call.
A week-ahead external consensus also centers on +0.3% m/m, so the model claims only a modest probability edge over even and no point-forecast edge over consensus.
The September 30 annual methodology update can revise history, so the target is the first-release August monthly change exactly as published.
surprising_if: Core PCE is <=0.1% m/m while contemporaneous growth remains resilient.

resolution.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, first Personal Income and Outlays release for August 2026, BEA 26-43, published September 30, 2026 at 08:30 EDT. At displayed first-release precision, August core PCE increased 0.2% month over month.
resolution.audit_note: Frozen original forecast preserved without hindsight alteration. The >=0.3% event resolved FALSE at the first-release 0.2%. Probability loss is worse than neutral; model point ties the frozen 0.3% consensus and has larger point error than frozen first-release July 0.2% context. That context is not a formally comparable skill benchmark because annual methodology changes may impair comparability. Today annual revisions changed July to 0.1%; that revised value must not replace the frozen 0.2% benchmark. Interval covers, which does not erase the event miss. August core prices are not a test of September energy pass-through. No learning claim.
